analysis:
Documentation-only PR; no executable code, wire protocol, or config changed. Examined docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (date bump plus new paragraph around head lines 334-339 on Autopilot placement holds removing slots from eviction snapshots and denying reclaim credit in free_for_load_gb) and docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md (new sections on adoption/hold placements, busy reasons, transition watchdog, invariants, failure modes).

Security-relevant claims described, not verifiable here because the Swift sources (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement, ProviderLoop+TransitionWatchdog, evictableModelSlots, autopilotServesModel) are not supplied: (1) Adoption lets a succeeded Autopilot operation's model serve without a live lease. The doc states it ends on consent revocation, deselection, failed self-test or unverifiable weight hash, and that it grants serving only, not prefetch or publication. This touches the consumed serving-authorization contract (TB-011, A-016, T-052/T-053), but the doc says the coordinator grants adoption/holds only to providers reporting matching capabilities, and does not change App Attest serving authorization. (2) Holds are bounded by hold_seconds, which is coordinator-supplied. A possible availability concern is that a hold could block eviction and cause load refusals; the doc says holds expire, are per-model, and are not machine-level control. The coordinator is trusted, so no finding. (3) The watchdog cancels only stalled operations and answers preload as failed without clearing flags, preserving memory-ownership fences, consistent with T-010 and the process-ownership invariants.

No observed regression in documented controls. Remaining integration question for the code-bearing PR: confirm the implementation matches the documented end conditions (reconcileAutopilotPlacements, hold-expiry, weight-hash verification before adoption) and that the hold cannot starve legitimate loads beyond the bound. The model-autopilot.md patch excerpt is truncated, but the base and head text cover the changes. Neither the threat model nor the TB-011 text needs updating from this documentation alone.
